results.text: The OCU400 DS is produced in HEK293 suspension cell culture using a production bioreactor-based manufacturing process. HEK293 cells are initially recovered and cultivated in an Erlenmeyer shake flask to initiate the seed train. The cell culture is expanded from the HEK293SF-3F6 working cell bank (WCB) and is performed through sequential scale-up of the culture volume. Following recovery, the cells are expanded through progressively larger shake flask cultures and intermediate seed expansion steps until the required cell biomass is achieved for inoculation of the production bioreactor. The upstream process is designed to support manufacturing across campaigns while maintaining consistent culture conditions and process performance. The upstream process flow for OCU400 production from GLP to PPQ scale is represented in Figure 3.

results.text: The purpose of the seed flask passage steps is to generate sufficient biomass of HEK293 cells for inoculation in the production bioreactor. Seed cultures are passaged at defined intervals under controlled conditions to maintain cell viability and growth characteristics. Subsequent seed flasks are inoculated at an appropriate viable cell density to support consistent expansion. Cells are sequentially expanded through culturing in a series of shake flasks and transferred to a seed bioreactor to generate adequate cell biomass for inoculation of the production bioreactor. The seed train strategy is scalable and designed to ensure consistent cell growth performance across manufacturing scales.

results.text: Following cell cultivation from cell passage 3, an in-process sample is withdrawn for determination of cell density and cell viability. If the cell density and viability meet in- process specifications, culture are pooled in one Erlenmeyer flask and redistributed according to defined volume in other Erlenmeyer flasks. The cell culture is mixed with pre- warmed BalanCD HEK293 medium containing 2% L-glutamine . An in-process sample is collected prior to incubation for determination of cell count, viability and morphology. The flask containing the cell suspension were placed in a CO2 incubator for cultivation for a defined cultivation period.

results.text: The production of OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) is based on triple plasmid transfection in HEK293 suspension cells with transgene phNR2E3, pRep2/Cap5, and pHelper plasmids. The phNR2E3 transgene plasmid is designed, synthesized, and characterized for identity and integrity of various regulatory elements (AAV2-ITR, CMV enhancer, CBA promoter, chimeric intron from rabbit globulin gene, and SV40 poly A). The rep gene sequence consists of wild type AAV2 serotype, and the cap gene sequence consists of wild type AAV5 serotype. The pHelper plasmid is used to provide various factors for AAV5 production in HEK293 cells. During research and development, Ampicillin antibiotic cassette was replaced with a kanamycin antibiotic cassette in all the plasmids (phNR2E3, pRep2/Cap5 and pHelper plasmids) and characterized for identity in plasmids produced during cGMP production. The purified plasmids were released against the specification.

Cell Passage 5: After 68 to 100 hours of cell cultivation, samples are collected from each flask and tested for cell density, viability, and morphology. The cell cultures obtained from cell passage 4 are transferred into six 3L Erlenmeyer flasks. Prewarmed BalanCD HEK293 medium containing (2% v/v) L-Glutamine (v/v) is added to each flask to make up final volume of 1728 mL. Prior to cell cultivation, 0.5 mL samples are collected from each 3000 mL Erlenmeyer flask and tested for cell density, viability, and morphology. The six 3000 mL Erlenmeyer flasks containing the cell suspension are placed in a CO2 incubator.

a. Pre-culture in 200 L Bioreactor:

While the Cell passage 4 is in progress, 50L BalanCD HEK293 medium is aseptically transferred into the 200L bioreactor. The bioreactor is run for pre-culturing and after 68 to 100 hours of cell cultivation of Cell Passage 5, a sample is collected from each of the 3L flasks to test for cell density and viability.

b. Inoculation in 200 L Bioreactor:

A feeding system is welded to the bioreactor bag and the pooled cell seed from passage 4 is inoculated to the bag using the compressed air. After 10-30 minutes of starting the culture, a sample is removed using a 50 mL sterile syringe for measuring cell density and viability.

c. First media addition:

After cultivation for 20 to 76 hours, if culture reaches the targeted cell density (1.0-1.6 x 106 cells/mL) and viability (≥85%), cells are fed with 25 L BalanCD HEK293 medium pre- warmed to 37±1℃. After 1 to 6 hours of culture, a sample from the bioreactor is removed for cell density and viability testing.

d. Second media addition:

After cultivation for 20 to 76 hours, if culture reaches the targeted cell density (1.6-2.0 x 106 cells/mL) and viability (≥85%), cells are fed with 25 L BalanCD HEK293 medium pre- warmed to 37±1℃.
